description: Figure 2 illustrates five distinct layer grouping patterns for a model divided into four groups (G₁ through G₄), arranged horizontally from left to right. Each pattern is represented by a small bar chart with four light green bars, where the horizontal axis corresponds to the group index (G₁ to G₄) and the vertical axis represents the number of layers assigned to each group. The five patterns, labeled beneath their respective charts, are: (i) “Increasing,” showing a progressive rise in bar height from G₁ to G₄; (ii) “Uniform,” with all four bars of equal height; (iii) “Decreasing,” showing a progressive decline in bar height from G₁ to G₄; (iv) “Spindle,” where the middle two bars (G₂ and G₃) are tallest and the outer bars (G₁ and G₄) are shortest; and (v) “Bottleneck,” where the middle two bars (G₂ and G₃) are shortest and the outer bars (G₁ and G₄) are tallest. The figure visually encodes how the number of layers per group varies across these five structural configurations.
